mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term decline in equity discount rates, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for ≥2 consecutive months prior to the window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (HOUST) signal weak labor market recovery, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when PAYEMS up and HOUST down.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above its prior month's level coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via stronger near-term economic momentum.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not predict 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.05) or returns are negative when INDPRO grows >2%.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months predicts a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates lower future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or no significant relationship (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL remains below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three months triggers a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate prolonged economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when UNRATE < 4% for ≥3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) above 150,000 while manufacturing activity (GDPC1) remains flat suggests wage pressure without demand expansion, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150000 and GDPC1 unchanged in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) under this interaction.

mechanism_narrative: INDPRO remains flat or declines for three consecutive months, reflecting weak industrial momentum and reduced near-term investment, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
Note: Since there is no retail sales series in the provided catalog, this is omitted. Instead, here's a valid supply proxy alternative using INDPRO: A prolonged flat or declining INDPRO (≥3 months) indicates weak industrial momentum, forecasting negative 20-day returns.
Correction: Let's use INDPRO as supply proxy for this one.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or statistically significant (p < 0.05) when INDPRO is flat or declining for ≥3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in FEDFUNDS to above 5% in the prior month combined with a sharp drop in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 200 triggers a regime shift: negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to heightened inflation fears.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and CPIAUCSL falls below 200 in the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline (p > 0.05) when both triggers are met.
